newsitem.title: USA: Sunbeam posts loss, completes first restructuring phase.
newsitem.headline: Sunbeam posts loss, completes first restructuring phase.

text.p: Sunbeam Corp. Wednesday reported a loss for the fourth quarter as the struggling appliance maker took hefty charges to implement a drastic restructuring.

The company, whose Sunbeam and Oster brands are household names, had a loss of $234.7 million, or $2.79 a share, in the quarter ended Dec. 29, compared with profits of $100,000, or no earnings per share, in the year-ago period.
Sales fell 5 percent to $268.9 million from $284.1 million, excluding the company's outdoor furniture product line, which has been identified for divestiture.
For full-year 1996, it lost $228.3 million, or $2.75 a share, compared with profits of $50.5 million, or 61 cents a share, in 1995. Sales slid 3 percent to $984.2 million from $1.02 billion.

Sunbeam Chairman Albert Dunlap announced in November plans to cut about 6,000 of the company's 12,000 workers, close 39 of its 53 plants and other facilities and eliminate 10,000 products, or nearly nine out of 10 of its products.

Dunlap, whose harsh measures have earned him the nicknames "Chainsaw Al" and "Nuclear Al," said Sunbeam had essentially concluded the cost cutting phase of the restructuring, to save $225 million, during the fourth quarter.

About 22 percent, or $75 million, of the restructuring and special charges were in cash, through payments of severance and other employee related costs, lease obligation and other plant costs associated with the rationalisation of facilities, it said.

The remaining restructuring and special charges are non-cash in nature, consisting mainly of asset and inventory write-downs, increases in several reserve categories and losses expected from divestiture of non-core businesses.

"Over the past few months, our goal has been to enter 1997 as a tremendously improved company, positioned for growth with a globally competitive cost structure. We have accomplished that goal in record time...," Dunlap said.

"In the next three years, our goal is to double the company's sales from $1 billion to $2 billion and to increase operating margins to 20 percent. We also have set a goal of tripling our international sales from under $200 million to $600 million over the same time frame."
Sunbeam also aims to achieve a 25 percent return on equity in each of the next three years and expects to be debt free by the end of 1997, he said.

The Delray Beach, Fla.-based company said it was also well into its brand repositioning strategy, led by a major new advertising campaign and new packaging. It said it will continue to advertise throughout 1997 at unprecedented levels.
Sunbeam's stock closed unchanged at $27.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
